texts.preamble: P. Sujitha vs The State Of Telangana And 3 Others on 5 May, 2022 Author: B. Vijaysen Reddy Bench: B.Vijaysen Reddy, D.Nagarjun High Court For The State Of Telangana The Hon'Ble Sri Justice B. Vijaysen Reddy And The Hon'Ble Dr. Justice D. Nagarjun Writ Petition No.5455 of 2022 Date: 05.05.2022 Between P. Sujitha. ... Petitioner And State of Telangana, Rep. by its Chief Secretary, Secretariat Buildings, Hyderabad and others. ...Respondents
texts.facts: 2. Cr.No.317 Nalgonda I U/s 386, 03.08.2021 in Detenu moved of 2021 Town PS 406, 420 Cr.No.301 of bail application Dt.16.08.21 and 506 2021 vide IPC read CRLMP.No.340 with of 2021 and the Section 34 same was IPC dismissed on 07.09.2021. Detenu moved second bail application vide CRLMP.No.376 of 2021 and was released on conditional bail dated 23.09.2021. 3. Cr.No.197 Gudipally U/s 420 03.08.2021 in Detenu moved of 2021 PS IPC Cr.No.301 of bail application Dt.16.08.21 2021 vide CRLMP.No.528 of 2021 and was released on bail. 6. According to the record, in all the three complaints, it is alleged that the detenu collected huge money from the complainants on the pretext of performing spiritual pujas, Homam with a promise to cure all personal, spiritual and health problems. 7. In Cr.No.301 of 2021, it is alleged that the detenu sought donation from the complainant towards construction of Sai Baba Temple by informing that they have applied for bank loan and it will take time for sanction of the loan and that money will be returned once the loan is sanctioned. When the complainant forced the detenu to return the money, she was threatened that her family will be destroyed by making sorcery and that his henchmen will kill her and her family members. In Cr.No.317 of 2021, it is alleged that the complainant approached the detenu seeking cure for the ill-health of his niece in October 2018. The detenu made believe the complainant to arrange the amount for performing pujas and promised to return the amount if his niece is not cured. The complainant gave Rs.6 lakhs for performing homam and thereafter, in total, collected Rs.18 lakhs. Meanwhile, on 06.09.2019, the niece of the complainant died and when they contacted the detenu, the complainant was threatened. In Cr.No.197 of 2021, the complainant got attracted to the detenu on seeing him in spiritual programs in the Bhakti TV Channel and approached the detenu seeking cure for the ill-health of his granddaughter. The complainant blindly believed the detenu and donated Ac.1.00 of land and thereafter, registered 10 acres of land in favour of the wife of the detenu. The detenu gave advance amount vide two cheques for Rs.5 lakhs to the complainant and later failed to pay remaining Rs.80,000/- The detenu convinced the complainant that money will be paid but was not paid till date. Vexed with the attitude of the detenu, the complainant lodged a complaint. The detenu did not return the money, as promised by her and thus, cheated them. The detenu was arrested in all the three cases; remanded to judicial custody and later released on bail. 8. The detention order points out that the incidents under the above referred crimes have caused loss of faith and trust among the general public. The detenu is responsible for cheating of huge hard earned money and valuable lands of innocent victims, who developed a hope that they would definitely get justice. Thus, it is opined that free movement of such offender is not safe in the interest of the society and there is imminent possibility of the detenu indulging in similar prejudicial activities, which is detrimental to public order, unless he is prevented from doing so by an appropriate order of detention.
texts.arguments: P. Sujitha vs The State Of Telangana And 3 Others on 5 May, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88707338/ 3 9. In RAM MANOHAR LOHIA v. STATE OF BIHAR1 it was held that contravention of law always affect order, but before it can be said to affect public order, it must affect community at large. The Apex Court considered three concepts law and order, public order and security of State and observed that to appreciate the scope and extent of each one of them one should imagine three concentric circles. The largest of them represented law and order, next represented public order and smallest represented the security of State. The Supreme Court held as under: "Does the expression "public order"' take in every kind of disorder or only some? The answer to this serves to distinguish "public order" from "law and order" because the latter undoubtedly takes in all of them. Public order if disturbed, must lead to public disorder. Every breach of the peace does not lead to public disorder. When two drunkards quarrel and fight there is disorder but not public disorder. They can be dealt with under the powers to maintain law and order but cannot be detained on the ground that they were disturbing public order. Suppose that the two fighters were of rival communities and one of them tried to raise communal passions. The problem is still one of law and order but it raises the apprehension of public disorder. The contravention of law always affects order but before it can be said to affect public order, it must affect the community or the public at large. AIR 1966 SC 740 In ARUN GHOSH v. STATE OF WEST BENGAL2 the Supreme Court held that: "It means therefore that the question whether a man has only committed a breach of law and order or has acted in a manner likely to cause a disturbance of the public order is a question of degree and the extent of the reach of the act upon the society. The French distinguish law and order and public order by designating the latter as order publique. The latter expression has been recognized as meaning something more than ordinary maintenance of law and order." The High Court of Judicature for the State of Telangana and the State of Andhra Pradesh in C. NEELA v. STATE OF TELANGANA3 held as under: P. Sujitha vs The State Of Telangana And 3 Others on 5 May, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88707338/ 4 "The State cannot find an easy way out by choosing to invoke the draconian provisions of preventive detention laws against every criminal as a substitute for his prosecution. As discussed supra, the Supreme Court has drawn a clear distinction between disturbance to public order on one side and disturbance to law and order on the other and held that only in the former case the State is permitted to invoke the powers under the preventive detention laws." 12. Right to life and personal liberty guaranteed under Article 21 of the Constitution of India cannot be deprived without following due process of law.
